subject: Private deployment: Enclave workbench module contracts & CI review

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment standard: Enclave workbench IaC contracts and CI

Hi Ava / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security and operations teams are aligned on using Redwood Private for a set of customer pilots, but they need a clear, auditable contract for each infra module (Terraform, Helm, Ansible) plus CI gate evidence before we can greenlight POC clusters.

Can you share your recommended module-contract template and a short checklist that your engineering org expects for a release gate? In particular, they asked for:
- explicit input/outputs for Terraform modules (no hidden assumptions)
- Helm value pinning and schema validation steps
- Ansible vault handling and least-privilege playbooks
- CI smoke test matrix (integration + upgrade path)

If you can send a one-page plan and an example contract that we can iterate on, that would help unblock procurement and scheduling. Attached is our internal template for context — feel free to adapt.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Shah
Platform Architect, EdgeCloud Solutions

Subject: Re: Private deployment standard: Enclave workbench IaC contracts and CI

Samir — thanks for the clear ask. We've sketched a lightweight contract and an internal CI gate checklist that map directly to what you listed. I attached the working templates so your team can comment inline. High level:

- Terraform modules: require a inputs.md and outputs.md per module, enforce explicit cidr/route contracts, and avoid provider-level side effects. We recommend a consumer-facing module (stable) and an implementation internal module (unstable) pattern.
- Helm: all customer-facing charts must include a values.schema.json and a pinned chart.lock file in repo. Chart upgrades go through a chartlint and dry-run stage in CI.
- Ansible: secrets in Ansible vaults or KMS-backed secrets; playbooks must run in no-op mode first and include idempotency tests.
- CI: gate requires 3 passing stages — unit (terraform validate/chartlint), gated integration (cluster create smoke + upgrade path), and a signed evidence artifact (s3/drive link) retained for audits.

Proposed next steps:
1) We iterate the attached module-contract-template.md with your template.
2) Karthik and I will scope the minimal smoke tests for your initial POC clusters.
3) Marissa will confirm an internal sign-off cadence and timeline.

Thanks — I reviewed the template and sketched concrete constraints we should enforce for the POC modules. Copying the relevant checklist here so it's captured in the thread: 

Terraform module expectations (POC minimal):
- Each module repo must contain: inputs.md, outputs.md, examples/, and a `no-side-effects` CI check that runs `terraform plan` against a disposable environment.
- Avoid data-sources that call external APIs at plan time; prefer remote state reads only.
- Enforce explicit resource tagging and a module_owner metadata field used by traceability tooling.

Helm expectations:
- values.schema.json required; CI runs `helm template --validate` + `ct` (chart testing) with pinned base images.
- Chart values that drive networking (service.type, hostAliases, egress) must be surfaced as top-level keys with clear defaults.

Ansible expectations:
- No plaintext credentials in playbooks; vaults must be backed by KMS in private deployments.
- Playbooks must be idempotent and have a `--check` smoke scenario executed by CI.

CI gating and evidence:
- Pipeline stages: lint -> unit tests -> helm/terraform dry-run -> ephemeral cluster integration -> upgrade test -> evidence bundle. Evidence bundle = test logs + manifest diffs + signed checksum. Bundle stored at the drive link below and referenced in the Jira ticket.
- Add a simple e2e that creates a single enclave (control-plane + 1 worker) and runs a health probe + token roundtrip. This keeps runtimes short (< 20m) but covers most regressions.

Operational notes:
- For Terraform, use workspace-per-environment naming; do NOT rely on implicit workspace defaults.
- For private deployments we'll prefer a cross-account S3 for state with explicit IAM roles per module.

Linking the Jira: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INFRA-7123 — I opened a checklist there and attached the template.

- POC scope: 3 modules (networking-vpc, enclave-controlplane, enclave-agent), 1 helm chart (controlplane), minimal Ansible playbooks for bootstrap only.
- CI gate: short smoke + upgrade path; evidence bundle uploaded to shared Drive folder (read-only to EdgeCloud).
